title: Exercise or Operation?
placeholderNote: Kordav and Elsin are fictional countries. All leaders, units and companies are fictional.

situation: You run the analysis cell for Task Force VEYL, the alliance's reassurance force in Elsin. Your customer is its commander, General Halvorsen.

The quarrel is over water. The Veyl rises in Elsin's highlands and irrigates Kordav's farmland downstream. Elsin controls the flow at Tarsk Dam, 6 km inside its border. The two governments have argued about it for ten years, and they sit down again tomorrow in Aubrec, the capital of neutral Pellaria.
Two days ago Kordav's 4th Army began its autumn exercise, IRON HARVEST, at the Ostrel training area, 40 km from the border. It holds one every year. Kordav says this one ends on the 20th.

customer.name: Gen. R. Halvorsen
customer.wants: Whether to move 2nd Battalion to the Tarsk sector. He commits as much as your confidence supports.
customer.context: Moving early is visible, and Kordav will call it provocation with talks under way. Moving late may not get there in time. A company can watch the crossing. It takes the whole battalion to hold the dam.

policySummary.action: Moves all of 2nd Battalion to Tarsk
Sends a reinforced lead company to Tarsk. The rest stays in garrison.
Holds position and leaves it to the diplomats
Relaxes posture and releases the reserve company to training

policySummary.brief: H1 or H3 at Medium or High with troops at Tarsk

replyLabels.deploy_company: Sends a reinforced lead company to Tarsk
replyLabels.deploy_battalion: Moves all of 2nd Battalion to Tarsk
replyLabels.upgrade_battalion: Sends the rest of the battalion to Tarsk
replyLabels.hold_company: Keeps the lead company at Tarsk and sends no more
replyLabels.frozen: Can't move while frozen. Raises readiness
replyLabels.relax: Relaxes posture and releases the reserve company

replies.deploy_company: Lead company of 2nd Battalion moves to Tarsk tonight, reinforced. That puts eyes on the crossing. It won't hold the dam. The rest of the battalion goes when your confidence is high, and not before.
replies.deploy_battalion: 2nd Battalion moves to Tarsk, all of it. If this turns out to be an exercise I will answer for it, so stay on it.
replies.upgrade_battalion: The rest of 2nd Battalion is moving up to join the lead company. That is everything I have for the sector.
replies.hold_company: Lead company stays at Tarsk. The rest of the battalion stays in garrison until your confidence is high.
replies.hold_battalion: The battalion is in position at Tarsk and staying there. Keep reporting.
replies.readiness: Readiness is raised. Nobody moves on low confidence. Bring me something firmer.
replies.hold: Understood. If it's posturing, the diplomats can answer it. We hold where we are.
replies.relax: Good. The reserve company goes back on the training rotation.
replies.withdraw: I'm bringing everyone back to garrison. I don't want to do this twice.
replies.frozen: I'm not permitted to move anything until the freeze lifts. Readiness is raised and your brief is on file.
replies.freeze: Kordav's delegation put photographs of my troops at Tarsk on the table before they walked out. Higher headquarters has ordered everyone back to garrison and frozen all movement for 48 hours. I moved early on your call, and it has cost us. Next time, be sure.

events.note: Your Day 3 and Day 4 briefs can't move the battalion. Your Day 5 brief can.

hypotheses.claim: IRON HARVEST is a routine exercise and units will go home on the 20th

hypotheses.text: The exercise hides preparations to seize Tarsk Dam.
hypotheses.claim: IRON HARVEST is cover for an operation to seize Tarsk Dam

hypotheses.text: A show of force to pressure Elsin at the talks, with no intent to cross.
hypotheses.claim: IRON HARVEST is a show of force to pressure Elsin, with no intent to cross

groundTruth.state: The exercise is real. Leadership enlarged it by 40% to gain leverage at the talks. 4th Army has drafted a contingency plan to seize Tarsk Dam (the "northern option"), but nobody has authorized it.

groundTruth.bestCall: H3 at Medium (H2 at Low is a defensible early warning)
groundTruth.state: The talks go badly. Contingency planning continues and is still not authorized. The delegation walks out that evening, after your brief.
Leadership authorized the northern option overnight. Orders go out at 0400: medical support and fuel move to operational accounts, comms security tightens and the cover story starts.
12th Brigade's lead elements and 77th Engineer Regiment (bridging) leave Ostrel for a hidden staging area near the Dolan crossing. 31st Brigade stays behind at Ostrel as the visible "exercise."
Final preparations. The bridging moves forward and the field hospital expands. The incursion is set for dawn on the 20th, the same day as the closing ceremony.

adversaryPlan.summary: A coercer wants to be seen. The threat is real messaging.
Once the operation is authorized, a visible threat only invites a defense, so Kordav switches to "routine."

sources.access: A clerk at 4th Army's fuel and supply depot in Varn, recruited eight months ago. He sees allocations, issue orders and account codes. He doesn't see unit plans. Meeting him is the risky part: don't task him two days running.
sources.postmortemNote: Stayed within his access all week. His one weak item was canteen talk, and he said so.

sources.access: Standing coverage of 4th Army logistics nets and some brigade voice nets.
sources.postmortemNote: The channel is reliable, but Kordav knew it was covered and staged one item on it.

sources.access: Commercial imagery. A standing daily pass covers the Ostrel training area and the river line. Forest and anything off that track has to be tasked. Needs clear weather.
sources.postmortemNote: Shows what's there and what isn't. Can't show intent on its own.

sources.access: Elsin's military intelligence. A long relationship. Elsin has been asking for months to have the task force at Tarsk.
sources.postmortemNote: Raises the alarm every day to get the battalion moved. Wrong on Days 1 and 2, right on Day 4.

sources.access: Kordav State Broadcaster and official ministry channels.
sources.postmortemNote: Accurate about what the state wants said.

sources.access: Continental Wire Service, an international news agency.
sources.postmortemNote: An honest outlet that went circular on Day 5.

sources.access: Social media monitoring. The accounts are unvetted.
Our own open-source team. Searches what you task it to.

reports.text:
Source reports: the depot's fuel allocation for IRON HARVEST is about 40% above last year's. Staff were told the increase came "from Army level" and were given no reason. It is booked to the standard exercise account.
Access: direct. He processes the allocation paperwork.
reports.postmortemNote: The scale-up was ordered for leverage. The exercise account code is the baseline that changes on Day 3.

reports.text: State television, last night's evening news. The defence minister, asked about the exercise on the eve of the Veyl talks: IRON HARVEST "shows Elsin that Kordav's patience has limits."
reports.postmortemNote: The minister links the exercise to the talks in public. That's coercive signaling working as designed.

reports.text:
Elsin's service assesses: Kordav will try to seize Tarsk Dam "within days."
Sourcing: none given.
Elsin asks that the task force move its forward battalion to the Tarsk sector at once.
reports.postmortemNote: Elsin's standing request dressed up as an assessment. It turns out roughly right later, for no reason anyone had on Day 1.

reports.text:
Ostrel training area, latest pass, clear skies.
About two mechanized brigades in field positions. The layout matches previous IRON HARVEST years.
Not seen: bridging equipment.
Dolan river crossing: no activity.
reports.postmortemNote: Fits every hypothesis, so it can't tell them apart. It's the baseline: note where things aren't (Dolan).

reports.text:
Dozens of posts from Kordav's capital since yesterday show long queues at filling stations. Several blame "military requisition." One mentions an outage at the Brenk refinery.
Unverified. No official statement.
reports.postmortemNote: The refinery outage caused the queues. Military fuel comes from depot stocks, not the capital's pumps.

reports.text:
4th Army logistics net, last 24 hours. Routine exercise traffic: fuel returns, vehicle states, ration strengths.
One reference to a "northern option" planning cell meeting at 4th Army HQ. Context not clear.
reports.postmortemNote: The contingency plan exists. Plans aren't intent: militaries draft options all the time.

reports.text: State television, live from Aubrec. The head of Kordav's delegation, arriving at the talks: "We came to listen. We did not come to wait forever."
reports.postmortemNote: Pressure rhetoric aimed at the table.

reports.text:
Elsin's service passes: its border posts report Kordavan reconnaissance patrols near Dolan overnight.
Sourcing: sightings from the border posts, at night.
Elsin repeats its request for the task force to move to Tarsk.
reports.postmortemNote: Routine Kordavan border-guard patrols, misidentified.

reports.text: Ostrel training area and the river line, latest pass. Heavy cloud. No usable imagery.
reports.postmortemNote: A collection gap. Not knowing is not evidence.

reports.text:
Source reports: the talk among depot staff is that "we're going across this time."
Source comment: they say this every year.
Access: canteen talk. He has seen no order or document.
reports.postmortemNote: Reliable source, worthless item. Grade the information, not just the source.

reports.text: From the embassy: a fisheries delegation from a third country requests a meeting with Task Force VEYL about trawler licensing. The task force has no trawlers and Elsin has no coast. The embassy asks who it should forward this to.
reports.postmortemNote: Nothing to do with the crisis.

reports.text: Aubrec: the Veyl water talks collapsed late last night. Kordav's delegation walked out after Elsin rejected a flow-sharing proposal. No date has been set to resume.
reports.postmortemNote: The trigger. The northern option was authorized within hours.

reports.text:
Source reports two orders received at the depot this morning.
(a) Send blood products and surgical supplies forward to a "field medical point." The depot was not told where.
(b) Move all IRON HARVEST fuel issues from the exercise account to a "contingency" account, effective 0400.
Access: direct. He saw both orders.
reports.postmortemNote: The best item of the day, and squarely within KESTREL's access. Exercises rarely push blood products forward, and operations are funded from different accounts than training.

reports.text: Defence ministry statement, read out on this morning's news: IRON HARVEST is "a routine, scheduled training event" that "will conclude as planned on the 20th." Kordav "remains committed to dialogue."

reveal.tell: Two days running, Kordav tied IRON HARVEST to the talks: "patience has limits" (R-1-02) and "we did not come to wait forever" (R-2-02). The morning after the walkout, the same ministry calls it routine. A coercer whose talks just failed has every reason to turn the pressure up, not down.

crossCheck.text: The same morning, KESTREL's depot pushed blood products forward and moved fuel to a "contingency" account at 0400 (R-3-02), and the logistics net went quiet at 0400 (R-3-04). A routine exercise needs neither.

reveal.motive: Once the operation was authorized, a visible threat only invited a defense. Kordav needed you to stop worrying, so it swapped the threat for "routine."

reports.postmortemNote: Compare with R-1-02 and R-2-02. The threat went quiet the morning after the walkout.

reports.text: 4th Army logistics net: traffic fell sharply after 0400 today. Several stations have moved to a net not seen before during this exercise.
reports.postmortemNote: Comms security tightened at 0400, the same time as KESTREL's account change. Two independent sources line up on the timing.

reports.text: A video with over a million views claims to show Kordavan tanks "heading for the border." It was filmed on the ring road around Kordav's capital, 300 km from the border. Kordav's National Day is the 28th.
reports.postmortemNote: National Day parade rehearsal.

reports.text:
Ostrel training area, latest pass, clear skies.
12th Mechanized Brigade: about half its vehicles are gone.
31st Mechanized Brigade: still in place.
Where the missing vehicles went is not visible on this pass.
reports.postmortemNote: Something big left Ostrel two days before the exercise was due to end. Where it went was only visible if you tasked imagery on Dolan (C-02).

pin.label: Half of 12th Bde gone from Ostrel

reports.text:
12th Brigade net, this morning, unencrypted voice: a company commander talks about "loading for return to garrison on the 20th."
Comment: this brigade has used encrypted voice for the whole exercise.

reveal.tell: 12th Brigade has used encrypted voice for the whole exercise. The one time it talks in the clear, it announces the cover story word for word. Real slips happen on routine chatter, not on the exact message the other side would want overheard.

crossCheck.text: The brigade's logistics nets went dark at 0400 on Day 3 (R-3-04), the opposite of an exercise winding down, and half of it has already left Ostrel (R-4-01), days before it's supposed to be 'loading for garrison.' Imagery of Dolan (C-02), if you tasked it, shows where it went.

reveal.motive: Kordav knew the net was covered. A reliable channel is the best place for a lie, because you trust the channel.

reports.postmortemNote: Staged for MERIDIAN. Reliable channel, planted content.

reports.text:
A post from an account claiming to be a 31st Brigade conscript: "Brigade-wide order today, exercise over, back to barracks on the 20th. Finally!" The photo shows soldiers packing.
The account was created three weeks ago and posts only about IRON HARVEST.

reveal.tell: A conscript wouldn't know a brigade-wide order with an exact date. The account is three weeks old and posts only about IRON HARVEST, which fits an account set up before the exercise for this job.

crossCheck.text: The post is about 31st Brigade, which imagery shows still at Ostrel (R-4-01). Even if 31st really does go home on the 20th, that tells you nothing about 12th Brigade, the half that has already left.

reveal.motive: Fill open sources with "going home" so the story seems to be everywhere.

reports.postmortemNote: A sockpuppet. A conscript doesn't know brigade-wide orders and dates. It's also about 31st Brigade, the one that isn't moving.

reports.text:
Elsin's service reports: Kordavan engineers seen near Dolan.
Sourcing: border police, in daylight.
Elsin says it will "act alone" if the task force does not move.
reports.postmortemNote: The same alarmist source as Days 1 and 2, but now imagery corroborates it. Corroboration should move you, not tone.

reports.text: Security office: phishing emails dressed up as travel office notices are going around. Do not open "Updated_Per_Diem_Rates.xlsm". The rates have not gone up.
reports.postmortemNote: Nothing to do with the crisis. Don't open it anyway.

reports.text: From Kordav's capital: "Kordavan forces will begin an orderly return to permanent bases by the 20th, defence sources say."

reveal.tell: Its key phrase, "orderly return to permanent bases by the 20th," matches the ministry press release word for word. Unnamed "defence sources" repeating a press release are the press release.

crossCheck.text: Read it next to the KSB release the same day (R-5-02): one origin, two items.

reveal.motive: CWS isn't lying. It repeated the ministry line, and Kordav got a second, more trusted voice for free.

reports.postmortemNote: Uses the exact wording of R-5-02 ("orderly return to permanent bases by the 20th"). The "defence sources" are the press release. Two items, one origin.

reports.text: Defence ministry press release: units will make "an orderly return to permanent bases by the 20th." The defence minister will attend a closing ceremony at Ostrel.

reveal.tell: Every "going home" item in this crisis comes through a channel Kordav controls or can feed: its ministry (R-3-03, R-5-02), an unencrypted call on a net it knows is covered (R-4-02), a new social media account (R-4-03) and a wire report quoting the ministry (R-5-01). Nothing independent backs it.

crossCheck.text: Units going home don't need blood products pushed forward on a contingency account (R-3-02), and half of 12th Brigade left Ostrel two days ago without going home (R-4-01). If you tasked imagery on Dolan (C-03), the bridging was 2 km from the river.

reveal.motive: The closing ceremony is real (R-5-03 shows the stands going up). Kordav wrapped the lie around a true event so it would check out.

reports.postmortemNote: Every "going home" item traces back to channels Kordav controls. Imagery says otherwise.

reports.text:
Ostrel training area, latest pass, clear skies.
31st Mechanized Brigade: still in place.
Parade ground: stands and flags going up for a ceremony.
Ground conditions: no snow cover anywhere in the area.
reports.postmortemNote: The ceremony is real: good deception wraps itself in true details. The bridging at the river was only visible if you tasked imagery on Dolan (C-03).

reports.text:
Source reports: the depot has been ordered to stop all fuel issues to 12th Brigade "until further notice."
He understands the brigade is now supplied "from somewhere else," and has been told not to discuss it.
Access: he saw the stop order. The rest is what his supervisor said.
reports.postmortemNote: 12th Brigade is on a separate operational supply chain and has been compartmented. KESTREL reports the limits of what he knows honestly.

reports.text:
A widely shared photo shows Kordavan tanks on rail flatcars at the Ostrel railhead, captioned "Going home!" There is snow on the vehicles and on the ground.
Original poster not identified.

reveal.tell: There's snow on the vehicles and on the ground.

crossCheck.text: The same day, imagery reports no snow cover anywhere in the area (R-5-03). The photo isn't from this week.

reveal.motive: An old photo costs nothing and spreads faster than any statement. This one is from last year's end of exercise.

reports.postmortemNote: Last year's post-exercise photo.

reports.text: From Kordav's capital: the central bank has raised interest rates by 50 basis points, citing inflation.
reports.postmortemNote: Nothing to do with the crisis.

reports.text:
Dolan forest, tasked pass, clear skies.
Fresh vehicle tracks and a cleared strip along the treeline.
No vehicles present.
reports.postmortemNote: The staging area being prepared. Nothing in the standing reporting showed it.

pin.label: Tracks and cleared strip, no vehicles

reports.text:
Dolan forest, tasked pass, clear skies.
About 30 bridging vehicles under the trees, 8 km from the crossing. Assessed as 77th Engineer Regiment.
Beside them: a tented facility consistent with a field medical unit.
reports.postmortemNote: The diagnostic item. Bridging hidden near a real crossing, with medical support forward. A show of force is meant to be seen, and nobody hides one in a forest. It also finds KESTREL's 'field medical point' (R-3-02).

pin.label: Bridging and medical tents in forest

reports.text:
Dolan staging area, tasked pass, clear skies.
About 40% more vehicles than on the previous pass.
Bridging vehicles have moved to within 2 km of the river.
The field medical facility has grown.
reports.postmortemNote: Final preparations for a crossing at dawn on the 20th.

pin.label: Bridging within 2 km of the river

reports.text:
Ostrel railhead, tasked pass, clear skies.
No rail cars staged. No loading activity.
reports.postmortemNote: Nobody was going home on the 20th. A cross-check against every 'going home' item.

reports.text: 4th Army HQ net: the "northern option" planning cell has gone to 24-hour manning.
reports.postmortemNote: Planning intensifying before anyone had authorized it. On its own it doesn't separate H2 from H3: militaries plan hard for options they hope not to use.

reports.text: 4th Army HQ nets: quiet. The stations we were following have moved to a net we don't cover.
reports.postmortemNote: The target went dark after the 0400 switch. Three points for a confirmation of R-3-04.

reports.text: Open sources: the defence ministry has cancelled the minister's foreign trip planned for the 21st. It made no announcement. The host country's press noticed.
reports.postmortemNote: The minister expected to be busy after the 20th.

reports.text: Rail enthusiast forums, which follow military traffic closely: no military trains are timetabled out of Ostrel before the 23rd.
reports.postmortemNote: A cheap cross-check against 'home by the 20th.'

reports.text:
At a meeting, source reports: two officers he didn't know asked the depot for fuel for "heavy vehicles" at a site the depot doesn't supply, north of Ostrel.
Access: direct. He took the request.
reports.postmortemNote: Fuel for the bridging column.

reports.text:
At a meeting, source reports: the "contingency" account now covers rations for 3,000 people for 10 days.
Access: direct. He saw the ledger.
reports.postmortemNote: Sustainment for an operation, not an exercise ending on the 20th.

reports.text:
In answer to our request: Elsin's service is certain an attack is imminent, and asks again for the battalion.
Sourcing: nothing new offered.
reports.postmortemNote: Elsin's standing agenda, free of charge and free of evidence.

reports.text: In answer to our request: Elsin's border police report engineers at the riverbank opposite Dolan.
reports.postmortemNote: Elsin is right once the facts catch up with it.

tellLabels.agenda-aligned: Lines up with the reporter's own agenda
tellLabels.different-cause: The item itself names a different cause
tellLabels.source-caveat: The source labels it as gossip
tellLabels.tone-shift: Sudden change of tone from the same speaker
tellLabels.location-mismatch: The location doesn't fit the claim
tellLabels.access-mismatch: The reporter couldn't have known this
tellLabels.new-account: New account that posts on one topic
tellLabels.circular-origin: Same wording as another item: one origin
tellLabels.recycled-media: Old media: snow that isn't there
tellLabels.too-on-message: Says exactly what the adversary wants you to hear

endings.title: Deterred
endings.text: At dawn Kordav's lead elements reach Dolan and find a battalion dug in on the far bank. They stop. By noon KSB reports that IRON HARVEST "concluded successfully," and the ceremony goes ahead with the minister in the front row. Nothing happened, so there is nothing for anyone to take credit for. Halvorsen sends the cell a two-line note anyway.

endings.title: Standoff
endings.text: 2nd Battalion is still on the road when Kordavan engineers bridge the river. They take the dam's access road. They don't take the dam. A week of negotiation follows, with Kordav holding ground it didn't hold before.

endings.title: Standoff
endings.text: The lead company holds the dam. Kordavan engineers bridge the river at Dolan and take the access road behind it, and the company is cut off. It is still on the dam when the talking starts again: a week of it, with Kordav holding ground it didn't hold before.

endings.title: Seized
endings.text: Kordav holds Tarsk Dam by 0900 and calls it "securing critical water infrastructure." The closing ceremony at Ostrel goes ahead on schedule.

script.text: For two days the threat was the message. Kordav enlarged the exercise to lean on Elsin at the talks, and said so on television. 4th Army had a plan for Tarsk, the "northern option," but nobody had authorized it. Elsin's service raised the alarm both days because it wanted the battalion at the dam. A warning at Low confidence was reasonable. Moving troops gave Kordav photographs to put on the table.

The walkout changed the answer overnight, and the order went out at 0400. KESTREL saw it at the depot: blood products sent forward, fuel moved to a contingency account. MERIDIAN saw it on the nets at the same hour. That morning the ministry, which had spent two days making threats, called the exercise routine.

Imagery showed half of 12th Brigade gone from Ostrel. If you had tasked Dolan, you knew where it went: bridging vehicles and a field hospital under trees, 8 km from the crossing. With KESTREL's report from the day before, that supported High. Without the Dolan imagery it was a harder call. Medium sent a company, and a company couldn't hold the dam. The unencrypted call and the conscript's post were put there for you to find.
Three reports said the troops were going home, and all three led back to the defence ministry. The photo of tanks on flatcars had snow in it. It was last year's.

lessons: A plan is not a decision. The "northern option" existed on Day 2 and meant nothing until it was authorized on Day 3.
Grade the report as well as the source. KESTREL is reliable, and on Day 2 he passed on canteen talk. MERIDIAN is reliable, and on Day 4 it carried a staged call.
Watch for a threat that stops. Kordav went from "patience has limits" to "routine" the morning its talks failed.
Confidence has consequences. Medium on Day 4 sent a company where a battalion was needed.
Count where reports come from. Day 5's three "going home" items had one origin.
Note what's missing. Half a brigade gone from Ostrel told you more than everything still parked there.
What you don't task, you don't see. Nothing in the daily reporting covered Dolan forest.

missedCollection.1: Imagery of Dolan forest would have shown a cleared strip with no vehicles yet: somewhere being prepared.
missedCollection.2: SIGINT on 4th Army HQ would have shown the 'northern option' cell going to 24-hour manning.
missedCollection.3: Imagery of Dolan forest would have found the bridging vehicles and the field hospital (C-02).
missedCollection.4: Imagery of the Ostrel railhead would have shown nothing loading: nobody was going home on the 20th.
missedCollection.5: Imagery of Dolan would have shown the bridging within 2 km of the river.

postmortem.openQuestion: Kordav staged a call on the one net we were reading, and its "routine" statement came out the morning after our assessment reached Kalsa. How did it know which net, and when?

policyNote: A company can watch the crossing. It takes the whole battalion to hold the dam.

countdown.label: the announced end of IRON HARVEST (the 20th)

dailyUpdates.text: IRON HARVEST is under way at Ostrel. Water talks open tomorrow in Aubrec, the capital of neutral Pellaria.
The talks open this morning. IRON HARVEST continues at Ostrel.
The talks broke up overnight. Both delegations have gone home, and no new date has been set.
No talks are scheduled. Elsin has put its border police on alert along the Veyl.
Kordavan state media is covering preparations for the end of IRON HARVEST.

map.legend: Plots reporting as it arrives, not confirmed fact. Dashed pins are items you doubted.

burnRules.text: KESTREL didn't come to the meeting. Our officer waited an hour and left.
burnRules.postmortem: KESTREL was tasked two days running. A depot clerk asking questions two days in a row gets noticed, and he went quiet.

pirs.question: Are 4th Army units moving toward the border outside the exercise area?
Has Kordav's leadership authorized action against Tarsk?
Is Kordav preparing to cross the Veyl (bridging, medical, fuel)?

levels.label: Trusted
levels.text: He acts on your confidence as given, with your full collection budget.

levels.label: Questioned
levels.text: His staff trims your collection: 1 point less a day.

levels.label: Discounted
levels.text: 2 points less a day, and he treats your confidence as one step lower: High gets the Medium move, Medium the Low one.

triggers.rule: He has to reverse a move he made on your word
triggers.note: Credibility −2. He moved troops on your call and was ordered to march them back.

triggers.rule: Your brief makes him pull back troops he sent on your word
triggers.note: Credibility −1. He sent troops on your call, and now your brief has brought them home.

triggers.rule: Low confidence two days running (each further Low day too)
triggers.note: Credibility −1. Low again. "That's two days of 'possibly'. I can't plan on it."

credibility.summary: Halvorsen can't see whether you're right until it's over. He can see when he has to undo a move, and when you won't commit.

grades.reason: raised the alarm on two days with nothing behind it

analysts.name: Imre Vasko
analysts.reveal: He settles on a reading early and fits what follows to it. His was coercion, which was right for two days. After the walkout he took each new item as the pressure campaign winding down.

analysts.name: Noor Halden
analysts.reveal: Careful, and slow. Her notes come a day after the item. She wasn't wrong once, and each time you had already briefed without her.

notes.text: I've watched this minister for years. When he wants something, he says it on television. This is aimed at the talks.
notes.why: Right on Day 1: it was signaling.

notes.text: 4th Army's staff writes a plan like this every couple of years. I wouldn't read more into it until someone signs one.
notes.why: Right on Day 2: plans aren't intent.

notes.text: The talks are off, so the pressure has nowhere to go. This is them climbing down. I'd expect units to start leaving Ostrel early.
notes.why: He took the plant as the natural end of his own theory. The same morning's depot and signals reporting said otherwise.

notes.text: WREN has raised the alarm twice this week with nothing behind it. I'd want more than border police before this went to the general.
notes.why: True, and beside the point: this time imagery agreed with them.

notes.text: CWS has it as well now. That's a second outlet with its own sources. I'd treat the withdrawal as confirmed.
Worth keeping this pass. No bridging at Ostrel and nothing at Dolan. If either changes, we'll want it to compare against.
For the record: yesterday's cloud means we saw nothing. It doesn't mean nothing moved.
notes.why: A gap isn't evidence either way.

notes.text: I checked the timing. The net went quiet at 0400, the same hour KESTREL's depot changed accounts. Those two sources know nothing about each other. That was an order going out.
notes.why: Two independent sources, one timestamp. It arrived a day after you needed it.

notes.text: I went back through the logs. Four days of encrypted voice from this brigade, then one unencrypted call, and it happens to be the ministry's line. I don't think that was a mistake on their part.
notes.why: The staged call. Her note came the morning after it was sent to fool you.

notes.text: Bridging under tree cover, with medical beside it. If this were for show, they'd have put it where we could see it.

caseFile.text: You doubted the call in the clear on 12th Brigade's net. It was staged on the one net we were covering.

deploy_company.text: Lead company of 2nd Battalion moves to Tarsk tonight, reinforced. That puts eyes on the crossing. It won't hold the dam. The rest of the battalion goes when your confidence is high, and not before. Understand the risk. Kordav will photograph it. If the talks go badly while my troops are on camera, higher headquarters will order them back, and I won't be able to argue.

deploy_battalion.text: 2nd Battalion moves to Tarsk, all of it. If this turns out to be an exercise I will answer for it, so stay on it. Understand the risk. Kordav will photograph it. If the talks go badly while my troops are on camera, higher headquarters will order them back, and I won't be able to argue.

upgrade_battalion.text: The rest of 2nd Battalion is moving up to join the lead company. That is everything I have for the sector. Understand the risk. Kordav will photograph it. If the talks go badly while my troops are on camera, higher headquarters will order them back, and I won't be able to argue.
